documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the pharmacy says my amlodipine needs a new script from you since the old doctor's ran out. I have about 5 left. Thanks, Randy L.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Got it - the 90-day supply with 3 refills went to your pharmacy. It should be there by the end of the day. Your Shingrix #2 is due next month; I put you down for Thursday 2/20 at 2:00.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second recombinant zoster dose, R deltoid. Afebrile. After dose 1 he had a sore arm and felt run down for about a day. Series now complete. Observed 15 min, fine on leaving.

documents.title: Leukemia program follow-up letter (received)
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Lindqvist on 03/19/2025 before his next maintenance cycle. He remains in remission and is tolerating azacitidine with venetoclax with the expected fatigue in the first week and occasional bone aches, for which he uses oxycodone sparingly. Feet unchanged. No infections since his last visit.

Exam unremarkable apart from reduced distal sensation in the feet. Port site clean. Counts adequate to proceed.

Plan: continue maintenance, same doses; acyclovir and posaconazole prophylaxis continue. Surveillance marrow in the fall. He knows to call us for any fever.

Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (hives).

Attending, leukemia program

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial AWV.

Interval: maintenance cycles continue, oncology visit 3/19 reassuring. No hospital stays. BP meds daily.

Health risk assessment (pt-completed form reviewed): lives alone, independent with daily activities and errands, drives. Hearing fine, vision fine with readers. No falls in the past year; feet numb, is careful on uneven ground. Diet ok, appetite dips in his injection week. Walks most days. Seatbelt, smoke detectors yes.
PHQ-2: 1. Cognition: conversation and recall normal, no concerns raised.

Meds reviewed, unchanged. Allergies: TMP-SMX anaphylaxis, contrast hives.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Oral mucosa clear. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abd soft. Feet: skin intact, no calluses or wounds; vibration/pinprick reduced to the ankles both sides, as before.

Prevention:
- Colon: 2020 colonoscopy normal, next 2030.
- Lung: LDCT eligible; still deferring during active leukemia therapy, revisit if treatment ends.
- Vaccines: flu, COVID, PCV20, Shingrix x2 done; Tdap 2019.
- Labs: CMP, lipids, A1c today.

Personalized plan given in writing. HTN f/u in the summer.

documents.title: Lab results from your wellness visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: All of Monday's labs came back in the normal range - kidneys, liver, sugar, cholesterol. Nothing to change. Enjoy the spring.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax: refill request for polyethylene glycol 3350 powder (17 g daily prn), last filled by prior PCP. Pt confirms still using on oxycodone days. Routed to PCP, approved, 1 container x 5 refills sent. Amlodipine has refills on file.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called, Wednesday is in the middle of his injection week at the cancer center. Cancelled and moved to Tue 8/5 at 2:40.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
BP f/u, rescheduled around his cycle.

Feeling fine this week. No headaches, chest pain or swelling. Hot summer, staying hydrated. Oncology plans a surveillance marrow in September. Uses oxycodone a couple times a month at most.

Vitals as charted; BP at goal. Looks well. Heart and lungs normal. No edema. Port site intact.

Plan: amlodipine 5 unchanged. Flu and COVID shots in early October around his cycle, nurse visit. See me in the winter, text sooner if needed.

documents.title: Leukemia program letter - surveillance marrow (received)
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Mr. Lindqvist had a surveillance bone marrow aspirate and biopsy on 09/09/2025. It shows continued morphologic remission of his AML. He tolerated the procedure well.

We reviewed the result with him on 09/17/2025. He remains on maintenance azacitidine with venetoclax 70 mg on days 1-14; acyclovir and posaconazole continue. Next cycle begins this month. Peripheral neuropathy of the feet is stable.

Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (hives).

Attending, leukemia program

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Seasonal Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Between cycles, afebrile. Inactivated flu (standard dose) L deltoid, 2025-26 COVID R deltoid. No issues during observation. Reminded him the leukemia line wants a call for any temp 100.4 or above.

conditions.label: Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia
conditions.note: febrile, ANC 100/uL, 3 weeks after last cycle

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Visit 12/10/2025, arrived 13:50.

CC: fevers and shaking chills x 2 days.

HPI: 55-year-old man with AML in remission on monthly maintenance chemotherapy at an outside cancer center; most recent cycle finished about three weeks ago. Two days of fever with chills at home. Sent in by the leukemia nurse line.

PMH: AML (intermediate-risk cytogenetics), hypertension, chemotherapy-related neuropathy of the feet. PSH: R chest port 2023, bone marrow biopsies (latest September), tonsillectomy.
Meds: acyclovir 800 mg BID, posaconazole DR 300 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, polyethylene glycol prn, oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn; maintenance azacitidine/venetoclax per oncology.
Allergies: SULFAMETHOXAZOLE-TRIMETHOPRIM - anaphylaxis. IODINATED CONTRAST - hives.
Social: ex-smoker 20 pk-yr, quit 2019; social alcohol.
Family: father lung cancer, mother DM2/HTN, paternal uncle acute leukemia.

Triage: T 38.9 C (102 F), BP 100/60, HR 110, RR 22.

Exam: pale. Mucosal ulcerations throughout the mouth. Port site without erythema. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rash. No other abnormal findings.

Labs: WBC 1.0 K/uL; ANC 0.1 K/uL (100/uL); Hgb 8.2 g/dL; Plt 50 K/uL. Blood cultures x2 (peripheral and port) drawn - pending at time of admission.

MDM: febrile neutropenia after chemotherapy with mucositis. Cefepime 2 g IV given after cultures. Oncology contacted; admit.

Dx: Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia with fever. Oral mucositis.
Disposition: admitted to the oncology service.

ED attending

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (received)
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - ONCOLOGY SERVICE DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 12/10/2025. Discharged 12/15/2025.

Principal diagnosis: febrile neutropenia due to chemotherapy (chemotherapy-induced neutropenia).
Secondary: oral mucositis; AML in remission on maintenance; hypertension; peripheral neuropathy.

Course: Admitted from the ED on IV cefepime, which was continued. Defervesced on hospital day 2. Blood cultures from the port and a peripheral site had no growth at 5 days. Mouth care and topical measures for mucositis; eating soft foods by discharge. Neutrophil count recovered over the stay and cefepime was stopped. Acyclovir and posaconazole continued throughout.

Discharge condition: stable, afebrile, ambulating.
Discharge medications: unchanged from home - acyclovir 800 mg BID, posaconazole DR 300 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, polyethylene glycol prn, oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn. Next maintenance cycle on hold until he sees his oncologist.

Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis), iodinated contrast (hives).

Follow-up: leukemia program in 1 week; primary care within 1 week.

Hospitalist, oncology service

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary in. Called pt. Home since Monday, no fever since the hospital, temp 98.6 this am. Mouth still tender but eating soft food and drinking well. Has all meds, no changes. Oncology appt 12/22. Booked with PCP Fri 12/19 at 10:40.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Admitted 12/10-12/15 for febrile neutropenia three weeks after his November cycle: ANC 100 in the ED, mouth ulcers, cultures negative, cefepime, counts recovered. Summary reviewed.

Now: no fevers at home, checking temp twice a day. Mouth much better, a couple of sore spots left. Appetite returning. Tired but up and about. Taking amlodipine.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. Looks tired but well. A few healing shallow ulcers on the buccal mucosa, no thrush. Port clean. Lungs clear, heart regular. No edema.

A/P:
- Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia, febrile episode, recovered: problem list updated. Oncology sees him Monday and will decide on the next cycle and dosing.
- Mucositis healing: salt-water rinses, soft diet a few more days.
- HTN: amlodipine 5, fine.
Meds reconciled, no changes. Fever precautions reviewed again. F/u per routine, text with any fever.
